The object manifest

Source: vignettes/object_manifest.Rmd
object_manifest.Rmd

A giotto object is large, deeply nested, and mostly opaque from the console. Two questions come up constantly and neither has a good answer from printed output:

  • What is in this object?
  • Did the step I just ran actually change anything?

objManifest() answers the first and manifestDiff() answers the second.

library(GiottoClass)

g <- GiottoData::loadGiottoMini("vizgen")
activeSpatUnit(g) <- "aggregate"

objManifest(g)
#> <gmanifest> schema 0.2.0
#>   uid: g-20261022190107-3e725d0987b6 | source: in memory
#>   cells: z0 498, z1 504, aggregate 462 | features: rna 337
#>   cell_metadata
#>     aggregate / rna
#>     z0 / rna
#>     z1 / rna
#>   dimension_reduction
#>     cells / aggregate / rna / pca / pca
#>     cells / aggregate / rna / tsne / tsne
#>     cells / aggregate / rna / umap / umap
#>   expression
#>     aggregate / rna / normalized
#>     aggregate / rna / pearson
#>     aggregate / rna / raw
#>     aggregate / rna / scaled
#>     z0 / rna / raw
#>     z1 / rna / raw
#>   feat_info
#>     rna
#>   feat_metadata
#>     aggregate / rna
#>     z0 / rna
#>     z1 / rna
#>   images
#>     dapi_z0
#>     dapi_z1
#>     polyT_z0
#>     polyT_z1
#>   nn_network
#>     aggregate / rna / sNN / sNN.pca
#>   spatial_enrichment
#>     aggregate / rna / cluster_metagene
#>   spatial_info
#>     aggregate
#>     z0
#>     z1
#>   spatial_locs
#>     aggregate / raw
#>     z0 / raw
#>     z1 / raw
#>   spatial_network
#>     aggregate / Delaunay_network
#>     aggregate / kNN_network

The manifest is what the object is. Its companion, objHistory(), records why it looks that way. The two are deliberately separate: the history is provenance, and object state is never reconstructed by replaying it.

Reading the inventory

slots holds one entry per non-empty slot, and each entry is a list of records, one per subobject. A record’s identity is under keys: the accessor arguments that retrieve it, and only the ones that apply. Everything else describes it: its class, its form, and a fingerprint of its content.

m <- objManifest(g)
str(m$slots$expression[[1]])
#> List of 5
#>  $ keys       :List of 3
#>   ..$ spat_unit: chr "aggregate"
#>   ..$ feat_type: chr "rna"
#>   ..$ name     : chr "normalized"
#>  $ class      : chr "exprObj"
#>  $ provenance : chr [1:2] "z0" "z1"
#>  $ dtype      : chr "dgCMatrix"
#>  $ fingerprint: chr "933e89d45e719a03b8c2231de99fc524"

Because the keys are the getter’s own arguments, a record maps straight onto a call:

rec <- m$slots$dimension_reduction[[1]]
rec$keys
#> $reduction
#> [1] "cells"
#> 
#> $spat_unit
#> [1] "aggregate"
#> 
#> $feat_type
#> [1] "rna"
#> 
#> $reduction_method
#> [1] "pca"
#> 
#> $name
#> [1] "pca"

pca <- do.call(getDimReduction, c(list(g), rec$keys, list(output = "dimObj")))
objName(pca)
#> [1] "pca"

Records report form and content, not size. Dimensions, row counts and extents are deliberately absent: on a disk-backed object each one costs a scan of the data. The counts that matter for reading a diff are in the summary block, which comes from the object’s id slots for free:

unlist(m$summary$n_cells)
#>        z0        z1 aggregate 
#>       498       504       462

Every field is read through its own guard. A field that cannot be read becomes NULL and its path is listed in warnings, rather than erroring the whole manifest: a state report that crashes is worse than no state report. On a healthy object the list is empty:

m$warnings
#> character(0)

Did my step do anything?

This is the day-to-day use. Take a manifest before the step, another after, and ask what moved:

before <- objManifest(g)

g <- createSpatialNetwork(g, name = "tutorial_net", method = "Delaunay")

manifestDiff(before, objManifest(g))$summary
#> [1] "spatial network added: tutorial_net"

Steps that overwrite something already present are the interesting case. Recomputing an existing network leaves its name and its place untouched, and only the content changes. The fingerprint is what sees it:

before <- objManifest(g)

g <- createNearestNetwork(g, name = "sNN.pca", k = 10)
#> > 'sNN.pca' already exists and will be replaced with
#>  new nearest neighbor network
#> Setting nearest neighbor network [aggregate][rna] sNN.pca
#> Setting nearest neighbor network [aggregate][rna] kNN.pca

manifestDiff(before, objManifest(g))$summary
#> [1] "NN network added: kNN.pca | NN network sNN.pca modified (directed, fingerprint)"

A step that changes the cells changes nearly everything at once. The count change is stated once and the records that moved with it are tallied, rather than listed one by one:

gs <- subsetGiotto(g, cell_ids = head(spatIDs(g), 100))
manifestDiff(objManifest(g), objManifest(gs))$summary
#> [1] "cells [z0]: 498 -> 100 | cells [z1]: 504 -> 100 | cells [aggregate]: 462 -> 100 | 27 objects changed"

manifestDiff() also returns changed (a flag) and detail (every affected record, as data). The one-sentence summary is what you would hand to a person, or a model; detail is what you would score or assert against.

Fingerprints

Every record carries a fingerprint: a short hash that changes when the content changes. Cell metadata goes one step further and fingerprints each column, so a diff names the column an edit touched, even an edit to a single cell that leaves the column’s levels unchanged:

before <- objManifest(g)

cm <- getCellMetadata(g, output = "cellMetaObj")
lv <- unique(cm[]$leiden_clus)
cm[]$leiden_clus[1] <- setdiff(lv, cm[]$leiden_clus[1])[[1]]
g_edit <- setGiotto(g, cm, verbose = FALSE)

manifestDiff(before, objManifest(g_edit))$summary
#> [1] "cell metadata changed: leiden_clus"

Level counts are not reported by default: counting the distinct values of every column is a full pass over the table, and the fingerprints already say which column changed. Ask for them with levels = TRUE and the diff says what a re-clustering produced:

cm2 <- getCellMetadata(g, output = "cellMetaObj")
cm2[]$leiden_clus <- cm2[]$leiden_clus %% 3
g_regroup <- setGiotto(g, cm2, verbose = FALSE)

manifestDiff(objManifest(g, levels = TRUE),
             objManifest(g_regroup, levels = TRUE))$summary
#> [1] "cell metadata changed: leiden_clus (5 -> 3 levels)"

How a fingerprint is computed depends on what the subobject holds:

Payload Fingerprinted from
matrices, tables, graphs, view and space steps all of their values, exactly
polygons and points a fixed-stride sample of the geometries and their attributes, plus the overall extent
images the pixels read at display resolution, plus extent and CRS
disk-backed stores the store’s handle: its identity, recorded operations and schema

A fingerprint is never a hash of the R object itself. Objects that hold an external pointer or an environment hash differently every time they are created, even when their content is identical; a fingerprint is built from the content extracted out of them. It is deterministic and never touches the RNG.

It costs little. In-memory content of half a million cells hashes in a few tens of milliseconds, and an image costs the same whatever its size.

Two comparisons are deliberately loose. Geometry coordinates are compared as a set of vertices to 12 significant digits, because writing a polygon to a shapefile and reading it back reorders its vertices and drops the last bits of a double. And images are read at display resolution, which uses a file’s overviews when it has them; so the same pixels saved in a format with overviews, such as a COG, fingerprint differently once.

Payloads GiottoClass does not know get their fingerprint from the package that provides them, through the fingerprint_data() generic. A payload with no method has no fingerprint, and the manifest says so in warnings. The diff says so too, instead of claiming nothing changed:

gu <- g
e <- gu@expression$aggregate$rna$raw
e@exprMat <- structure(list(), class = "someNewFormat")
gu@expression$aggregate$rna$raw <- e

mu <- objManifest(gu)
mu$warnings
#> [1] "expression.aggregate.rna.raw.fingerprint"
manifestDiff(mu, objManifest(gu))$summary
#> [1] "no detected change (1 item unfingerprinted)"

The history log

ghistory_records() returns the object’s history as structured records rather than printed text:

g <- subsetGiotto(g, cell_ids = head(spatIDs(g), 100))

str(tail(ghistory_records(g), 1)[[1]], max.level = 1)
#> List of 8
#>  $ step_id  : chr "19_subset"
#>  $ fn       : chr "subsetGiotto"
#>  $ params   :List of 12
#>  $ timestamp: chr "2026-10-22T19:01:12Z"
#>  $ seed     :List of 2
#>  $ status   : chr "ok"
#>  $ error    : NULL
#>  $ diff     : NULL

params holds the arguments the function actually ran with, as deparsed expressions, so 1:30 survives as "1:30".

Not every change is logged, though. Only a minority of the suite’s functions call update_giotto_params(), and a direct slot assignment calls nothing at all, so an object’s contents can move with nothing in its history claiming responsibility. recordGiottoStep() closes that gap for a caller that can see the change happen:

before <- objManifest(g)

cm <- getCellMetadata(g, output = "cellMetaObj")
cm[]$hand_label <- rep(c("tumor", "stroma"), length.out = nrow(cm))
g <- setGiotto(g, cm, verbose = FALSE)

d <- manifestDiff(before, objManifest(g))
d$summary
#> [1] "cell metadata added: hand_label"

g <- recordGiottoStep(g, fn = "manual annotation",
                      status = "unattributed", diff = d$detail)

tail(names(objHistory(g)), 1)
#> [1] "20_unattributed"

A failed call is recordable the same way, with status = "error".

On disk

saveGiotto() writes two sidecars beside the object: manifest.json (what it is) and history.ndjson (why, one operation per line).

td <- file.path(tempdir(), "manifest_vignette")
dir.create(td, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

saveGiotto(g, dir = td, foldername = "mini", verbose = FALSE)

saved <- file.path(td, "mini")
list.files(saved)
#> [1] "Features"       "gobject.RDS"    "history.ndjson" "Images"        
#> [5] "manifest.json"  "SpatialInfo"

The point of the sidecar is that it answers questions about the object without loading it:

sc <- jsonlite::fromJSON(file.path(saved, "manifest.json"),
                         simplifyVector = FALSE)

unlist(sc$summary$spat_units)
#> [1] "aggregate" "z0"        "z1"
unlist(sc$summary$n_cells)
#>        z0        z1 aggregate 
#>       100       100       100
vapply(sc$slots$expression, function(r) {
    paste(r$keys$spat_unit, r$keys$name, sep = "/")
}, character(1))
#> [1] "aggregate/normalized" "aggregate/pearson"    "aggregate/raw"       
#> [4] "aggregate/scaled"     "z0/raw"               "z1/raw"

Fingerprints survive the round trip: an object saved and loaded back has the same fingerprints as the one that was saved, so a diff across a save reports only what actually changed.

objManifest_json() and objHistory_ndjson() produce the same two documents for any object, whether or not you are saving it. The JSON follows a versioned schema that ships with the package:

system.file("schema", "giotto-manifest-0.2.0.json", package = "GiottoClass")
#> [1] "/home/runner/work/_temp/Library/GiottoClass/schema/giotto-manifest-0.2.0.json"

Records are sorted by their keys so two manifests of the same state serialize identically, and NA, NaN and Inf are encoded as strings so that a missing value stays distinguishable from a not-a-number.

What it is good for

  • Checking that a step did what you expected, and noticing when it did nothing.
  • Inspecting a saved object without loading it.
  • Regression-testing a pipeline: same inputs should give the same fingerprints.
  • Diffing two runs, or the same analysis before and after a parameter change.
  • Turning history.ndjson into a methods section.
  • Giving an assistant, an eval harness or a reviewer machine-readable state instead of printed text.

What it does not do

  • Sizes are not reported. Dimensions, row counts and extents would each cost a scan on a disk-backed object, so records carry none; the summary block’s cell and feature counts are the exception.
  • Sampled payloads can miss a local edit. Moving one polygon that falls outside the geometry sample, or painting a few pixels between the points an image is read at, can leave the fingerprint unchanged. Matrices, tables and graphs are hashed in full and have no such gap.
  • Disk-backed payloads need a method. A store is fingerprinted only once the package that provides it implements fingerprint_data(). Until then it is listed in warnings and the diff counts it as unfingerprinted.
  • The history is not complete by construction. It records what functions chose to log. Entries written with toplevel = 1 name update_giotto_params rather than the calling function, a property of those call sites, not of the record.
  • The schema is 0.2.0 and not yet released. Treat the field set as stable in spirit, not frozen.
